tieu_de: An Tong An Quang Van Sao Tuc Bien
tom_tat: The Pure Land Dharma is so great that [nothing] can go outside [its scope], like the sky that covers everything, like the earth that lifts evenly. There is no dharma that has not been established from this dharma, no one that has not been molded by this dharma. Because of all the dharmas…
noi_dung:
An Tong An Quang Van Sao Tuc Bien

The Pure Land Dharma is so great that [nothing] can go outside [its scope], like the sky that covers everything, like the earth that lifts evenly. There is no dharma that has not been established from this dharma, no one that has not been molded by this dharma. Because all the Mahayana and Hinayana dharmas that the Tathagata has spoken about throughout a lifetime, they all depend on the nature of sentient beings, or they are in agreement but cannot be in agreement with all abilities; or the contract cannot be in accordance with the ultimate reason (ultimate reason) thoroughly. Therefore, the Tathagata's nature to save sentient beings is hidden and has not yet been understood, and the great dharma that allows sentient beings to attain liberation in this life is still hidden and has not been revealed. Although the Hoa Nghiem [Dharma Assembly] has guided the West, the people of Humanity, Heaven, and Right Vehicle [Bodhisattva] have not heard it. The sutras also often outline good clues, but the outline of the method has not been laid down. Therefore, the Tathagata aroused the heart of Unconditioned Compassion, mobilized the mind of Oneness of Compassion, in the Assembly of Equality, especially spoke the three Pure Land Amitabha Sutras, pervading the three senses, absorbing all nine precepts, extolling the Tathagata's universal enlightenment and enlightenment, teaching sentient beings on a great scale "the mind does, the mind is". Both reason and mechanism are in harmony, both mortals and saints benefit from it, like the medicine Agada cures all diseases, like the emptiness of the ten directions that encompasses all images, causing all saints and ordinary people to achieve their karma in the present life, clearly revealing the Tathagata's eternal nature to save birth! If the Tathagata had not spoken this Dharma, no sentient being in the Dharma Ending Age would be able to escape birth and death in this one life.

His karma was heavy, he was born in the place where the Dharma was destroyed, and after only half a year of birth, he suffered from a closed-eye disease for six months. When he was at school age, he encountered many scenes of robbers and soldiers harassing him. Just having a little understanding, he was exposed to Trinh and Chau's poison of defaming Buddha. Fortunately, there is absolutely nothing in education, and it is impossible to create the karma of falling into Avici while still alive. If we were as intelligent as them, we would commit crimes that would be unforgivable in the ten directions. Due to that evil intention, he suffered from a long-term illness, for several years, like a disabled person. One day, he realized he had gone astray, so he left home to become a monk, hoping to destroy his sins. Tong - Deep teachings without the strength to study, the great Pure Land religion is determined to follow, intending to be a monk who only knows how to eat and drink, only worries about self-help, and has no dream of propagating the Dharma to benefit sentient beings!

At the age of thirty-three, when he came to Phap Vu pagoda on Pho Da mountain, the Abbot, Venerable Hoa Van, knew that Quang only knew how to eat and couldn't do anything else, so he made him a regular customer, not entrusting him with any trivial matters. Over the past twenty years, I have been quite peaceful, throughout the year no one came to visit me, I did not receive any letters.

In the third year of Tuyen Thong (1911), the Buddhist newspaper Tung Bao was published in Shanghai. Mr. Gao Hac Nien sent the newspaper several times by post to show him. Seeing that the writings printed in that newspaper were mostly fair, but the political abuses in the newspaper were somewhat biased, I was afraid that someone would use that story to ridicule Buddhism, so I used the name Van Thuy Tang Thich Thuong Tam to send a letter asking the journalist to argue fairly and not let the beautiful gems have blemishes, but the editors did not pay attention. Later, Mr. Hac Nien went to this mountain, I told him the whole story; He then published a few manuscripts in the newspaper, signed with the name Thuong Tam, no one knew about them.

In the sixth year of the Republic of Vietnam (1917), Mr. Tu Uy Nhu received three letters from friends, so he printed out five thousand copies, titled An Quang Dharma Master Tin Cao (manuscript of letters from Dharma Master An Quang) and gave them to everyone. In the seventh year of the Republic of China (1918), he collected more than twenty more letters, printed them in Beijing, titled them An Quang Dharma Master Van Sao, and brought that book to Putuo to seek refuge. Quang told him to take refuge with De Nhan. In the eighth year of the Republic of Korea (1919), Tuc Bien was published again. In the fall of that year, his mother died at her residence in Than (Shanghai). After the funeral was over, he asked Thuong Van An Thu Quan to combine So Bien and Tuc Bien into one. In the 12th year of the Republic of Vietnam (1923), Quang told the Thuong An Thu Quan Department to separately print the Tang Dinh version, divide it into four volumes, and save the 1st edition. The first time, printing 20,000 copies. In the 14th year of the Republic of China (1925), the China Library Department again printed the Tang Quang edition, still divided into four volumes. From then on, no matter what the writing was, no drafts were left behind, firstly so as not to waste the benefactor's money, secondly so as not to offend the wise eyes of wise people. In the 19th year of the Republic of China (1930), the guard at the Bao Quoc Pagoda in Suzhou, the Duong

Tang Dinh Ban later added a few more articles, so it was called Tang Quang Chanh Bien, or An Quang Van Sao So Bien. “Save copy” means to keep the printed copy. At that time, printing was often done using woodblocks. Wooden plates with engraved letters were very cumbersome, so if not requested, the printing house would not keep the woodblocks.

Gia2 [that pagoda] is the teacher Minh Dao for people to copy and steal. In the 24th year of the Republic of Korea (1935), he passed away.

In the 26th year of the Republic of Vietnam (1937), Quang took refuge in Linh Nham Son. The scribe gave the copy to the Duong Gia [Linh Nham pagoda], master Dieu Chan. Master Dieu Chan had it copied and published in semi-monthly magazines. Quang knew, but he was in a situation where he couldn't do anything. He could only carefully review it to print it to satisfy his teacher. Quang was poorly educated when he was young. When he grew up, he knew nothing. His writing was very clumsy and simple, not worthy of attention. But what Quang said was based on the meaning of the Buddhist scriptures and the words of the Patriarchs, then he simply said it as he saw fit, not daring to give rise to false opinions that would mislead people, and added what he had experienced for more than fifty years. If you are willing to ignore the text to grasp the meaning, you can certainly consider it as a wooden marker to point directly to the story of returning to the West (returning to the Western Pure Land) without any hesitation! Please devote all your strength to the West, courageously moving forward. Just because this wooden marker is ugly and despicable doesn't mean you don't want to see the route to the West, neither the person who built the marker nor the person who returned to the West will regret it.

In addition, although the Short Bien series has been printed in more than 100,000 volumes, the most knowledgeable people see that this book only talks about "faith and vows to recite the Buddha's name, cause and effect retribution, keeping morality intact, taking care of all duties, educating the family", which are all simple words of advice for life, not at all the words "pulling back the clouds to see the moon, opening the door to see the mountains", expanding people's minds, and clearly revealing the Buddha's nature, so it is considered trash. There are also people with the same nature as Quang, who view [this book] as a wonderful treasure. Because of this, there are many people who abandon delusion and follow enlightenment, abandon evil and return to righteousness, live with integrity, and are reborn in the Pure Land. The Tuc Bien, in addition to what was said in the So Bien, also added stories such as “[advising] pregnant women to chant Quan Am, poisonous milk kills their children”. These are all things that monks and doctors have never mentioned before, but Quang keeps repeating them.

If the ancients were not good generals, they were also good doctors, only wanting to help people and save lives. Quang is an ignorant and unconscious monk who only knows rice and porridge. Because Mr. Tu Uy Nhu alone spread his false reputation, in the end, many people received the false reputation, welcomed the echo, considered it real, and considered him a wise man. They have "spread false lies" and Quang is not afraid to "use them

Duong Gia in its original meaning is the butler of a mansion or a palace. The pagoda also uses the word Duong Gia to refer to the monk who manages a temple. Monk Dieu Chan has been the Duong Gia since monk Chan Dat became abbot of Linh Nham.

"Teaching the living to have a place to rely on, to have a place to rely on when they die, to give birth without trouble, to have children not die sideways, to take full advantage of my heart. Even though it hurts the wise eyes of the wise, because it is beneficial to people and does not cause harm to the world, so according to the wishes of the two masters Minh Dao and Dieu Chan, [this book] is circulated and summarizes dependent origination. Understand me or accuse me of my sins, it doesn't count like that!

Year of the Republic of China 28 (1939), Ky Mao, early Summer,

Thuong Tam Quy Monk Thich An Quang respectfully composed (at the age of 79)

Master Yinguang Mage

Van Sao Tuc Bien

tieu_de: 1. A letter sent everywhere
tom_tat: (Although the words are clumsy and simple, the meaning is originally taken from the Buddhist scriptures. If you follow them, the benefits will be immense. Year of the Republic of China 21 -
noi_dung:
1. A letter sent everywhere

(Although the words are clumsy and simple, the meaning is originally taken from the Buddhist scriptures. If you follow them, the benefits will be immense. Year of the Republic 21 - 1932)

The Pure Land Dharma, which covers all three senses, benefits and dulls the whole, is the great Dharma for the Tathagata to universally save all saints above and below, making them end birth and death in this one life. Isn't it sad if you don't believe in this Dharma, don't practice it? This method takes the three dharmas of Faith - Prayer - Virtue as its main principles3. Faith is believing that our world is suffering, believing that the world of Ultimate Bliss is happy. Believing in me is the karma of ordinary people, so we cannot rely on Self-Power to cut off or realize the Truth in order to escape birth and death. Believe that Amitabha Buddha has great vows; If there is a living being who recites the Buddha's name and wishes to be born in a Buddha land, when that person dies, the Buddha will be kind enough to take him to the West. I wish to quickly escape this world of suffering, I wish to quickly be reborn in that world of Ultimate Bliss. Hanh is to be sincere and earnest, constantly reciting Namo (pronounced Nap-mac4) Amitabha Buddha, don't forget it temporarily at the right moment. Morning and evening, worship and chant before the Buddha, depending on whether you are free or busy, set up a course5. In addition, [while] walking - standing - sitting - lying down and doing things that do not require the use of the mind, all should be skillfully remembered. When sleeping, you should recite silently, not out loud. You should only recite the four words Amitabha Buddha to avoid many difficult words

Tongue: Tone here is the main meaning of a sutra, or the main policy or teaching promoted by a sutra. Understood in a broad sense, Tong is the basic and main teachings of a dharma. According to Thien Thai Tong, Tong is the consistent content of a sutra or a dharma.

Because the word Namo 南無, if read in a normal Mandarin accent, will become Nán-wú, so here the Patriarch recorded it with the word Nap-mac 納莫 (Mandarin pronunciation is Nà-mó) to indicate a reading simulating the Namo sound in Sanskrit.

Course: A certain period of practice in a day, often used to refer to a period of chanting sutras, reciting Buddha's name or meditating.

concept. If your clothes and hat are not neat, or you are washing, urinating, or going to an unclean place, you should recite it silently. Reciting silently has the same merit [as reciting out loud], reciting out loud is not appropriate. Regardless of whether you recite loudly or softly, recite Vajra (reciting with sound but the person next to you cannot hear), recite silently in your mind, you must recite clearly and clearly in your mind, recite clearly with your mouth, and clearly with your ears. In this way, the mind does not wander outside, delusions gradually stop, Buddha's thoughts gradually become pure, and the merit is great!

People who recite Buddha's name must be filial and take care of their parents, serve their elders (i.e. teachers and virtuous people), be compassionate and not kill (should be vegetarian, or fast. If you have not stopped eating salty food, do not kill yourself), practice the Ten Good Karmas (i.e. do not commit physical acts of killing, stealing, or adultery; do not use your mouth to lie, embellish, double-talk, or speak evil words; your mind must not give rise to thoughts of lust, anger, or stupidity). There must also be a benevolent father, a filial son, a yielding brother, a respectful younger brother, a harmonious husband, an obedient wife, a benevolent master, a loyal servant, and taking all of one's duties seriously. No matter whether others have fulfilled their duties to us or not, we must always fulfill our own duties. If one can show all gratitude and duty to one's family and society, one is called a "good person". Good people who recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the West will surely be reborn immediately when they die because their mind is united with the Buddha, so they feel the Buddha's kindness and guidance. If, although you often recite the Buddha's name, your mind does not follow the Dharma, or if you cannot fulfill your duties towards your parents, siblings, concubines, children, friends, or neighbors, then your mind has gone against the Buddha and it will be difficult for you to be reborn! Because obstacles arise from the mind, the Buddha has no way to be compassionate enough to guide him!

You should also advise your parents, brothers, sisters, concubines, children, neighbors, and friends to regularly recite "namo Amitabha Buddha" and "namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva" (every day if you recite ten thousand verses of the Buddha's name, then recite five thousand verses of Avalokiteśvara, more or less according to this and decrease). Because this benefit is so great, how can the person who gave birth to me and my relatives and friends not enjoy this benefit? What's more, right now is a time of great tribulation in the world, disasters that cannot be dealt with. If you often recite Buddha's name and Quan Yin, you will definitely receive Buddha's protection and evil will turn into good. Even if there is no accident, karma will be eliminated, wisdom will clear, obstacles will be eliminated, and blessings will increase. What's more, advising people to recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the West is an achievement for ordinary people to become Buddhas, great merit! If you use this merit and dedicate it to rebirth, you will surely be satisfied.

Everyone who chants sutras, chants mantras, worships, repents, saves accidents, helps the poor, all charitable merits must be dedicated to rebirth in the West, and should not pray for blessings from humans and heavens in the next life. If you have that mind, there will be no rebirth! As long as birth and death are not resolved, the greater the blessing, the heavier the karma. Whenever one is born again, it is difficult to avoid falling into the three evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. If you want to regain your human body and meet the Pure Land dharma and attain liberation in one lifetime, it's as difficult as going to heaven! Buddha taught people to recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the West so that people can escape birth and death in this life. If you pray for blessings to be rewarded by humans and heaven in the next life, it is against the Buddha's teachings. It's like exchanging a priceless pearl in the whole world for a sugar card to eat. Isn't that a pity? Stupid people who recite Buddha's name do not seek rebirth in the West, nor do they pray for blessings in the next world!

People who recite Buddha's name should not abuse the Zen path of investigation, because those who study do not focus on faith and prayer for rebirth; Even when reciting Buddha's name, we only focus on observing the question "Who is the person reciting Buddha's name?" Just to ask for enlightenment! If born in the West, no one would not be enlightened! If you become enlightened and your karma is completely wiped out, you can end life and death. If Or karma is not exhausted, you will not be able to rely on Self-Power to end birth and death. Because we do not have faith and vows, we cannot rely on Buddha's power to end life and death. Neither Self-Power nor Buddha-Power can be relied upon. Is it possible to escape reincarnation? You must know: When the Dharmakaya Bodhisattva has not yet become a Buddha, he must rely on the power of the Buddha, not to mention the karmic power of ordinary people who waste time discussing Self-Power and do not rely on the Buddha's Power? Although the words are noble, the conduct is vile. The power of Buddha and Self-power, big and small, are not as different as the sky and the abyss! May all fellow workers6 understand this meaning.

People who recite Buddha's name should not imitate fools and do "Buddhist things" such as returning to life7, depositing treasures, etc. because the story of "returning to life" does not come from Buddhist scriptures, but was fabricated by later generations. “Depositing” means wishing to die and become a ghost, preparing money to spend in the devil world. If you have a wish to become a ghost, it will be difficult for you to be reborn. If you haven't done it yet, don't do it

Fellow people: People who have the same foundation as us.

This is a superstitious view of ancient Chinese people. They believe that when born as a human, everyone owes a sum of money in the underworld. If they do not burn paper money and beg to pay the debt, they will gradually lose their blessings, shorten their life, encounter many accidents and nightmares, and their souls and seven souls will be weakened and die prematurely. Burning gold and silver paper money to pay off debt is called Complete Tho Sanh (this view is promoted through the apocryphal Tho Sanh). "Storing" means burning paper money, gold and silver to store it in the underworld as a form of saving money for use after death.

do. If you have done so, please tell the Buddha clearly: "The disciple named... only prays for rebirth. The money previously deposited in the underworld is all used to diagnose the soul" then it will not cause obstacles to rebirth. All sutras such as Tho Sanh, Huyet Bon, Thai Duong, Thai Am, Nhan Quang, Kitchen God, Thai Cot, Phan Chau, Dieu Sa8, etc. are all fabricated by misguided people.

The Sutra of Life is a sutra fabricated by Taoism. The content of the sutra says that in the year Trinh Quan of the Tang Dynasty, Mr. Xuanzang reviewed the Tripitaka and found it clear that every person who was reincarnated as a human owed a large debt to the underworld, and the underworld official would search for that person in the human world to collect the debt. Anyone who refuses to pay that debt by burning paper money and joss paper to pay the debt to the underworld will have many nightmares at night, their three souls and seven souls will be lost and defeated, and they will suffer from eighteen kinds of disasters such as being robbed on the road, having difficulty giving birth, dying suddenly, being hit by wind and dying, dying from epidemics, car accidents, being falsely accused, arrested, imprisoned, disabled, etc. If anyone diligently pays their life debt, they will be rewarded. full of happiness, no disasters, no bad stars, three generations of wealth, never poverty, bad speech, etc.

The Blood Tank Sutra (full name is the Blood Tank Sutra of the Buddha's Teachings of the Great Tripitaka) says that Maudgalyayana went to Truyen Duong district in Vu Chau and saw a hell in the shape of a large blood basin up to eighty-four thousand yojanas wide, with all the instruments of execution. In the prison, there were many women with droopy hair who were forced by the guards to drink blood three times a day. If you refuse to drink, the devil will brutally beat you with an iron rod. When asked about the reason, the demon replied: "Because the woman was giving birth or having her period, dirty blood seeped into the ground, offending the earth god. Or bathing caused river and stream water to be contaminated with dirty blood. Others did not know how to use that water to make tea to offer to saints and sages, so the Great General recorded that person's crime. After death, she fell into this hell. If you want to save the mother's soul, you must recite this sutra for three years, set up a Blood Tank to win the assembly, invite the Sangha to recite this sutra, and the mother's soul will be liberated. escape!”

The Sutra of the Sun (full name is Sun Tinh Quan Bao Cao), has the content of praising the sun god, I would like to quote a passage such as: "Dong Duong is the most holy, Yen Ming Thuong Tru, the owner of the South Pole, the body and soul, the light and greatness, the conduct of all things is noble and virtuous, the dominant force shines on the lives of living beings, shining back on heaven and earth, the divine light resides at night, surrounds the yin and yang, the Yin-yang is majestic and fierce, the light shines on the world. reborn as, great compassion, great vow, great saint, great mercy of the Sun Palace, Sunlight, Grace, Universal Light, Shining Heavenly Venerable" (temporary translation: Sun Palace, Grace, Universal Light, Shining Heavenly Venerable, great compassion, great vow, great saint, great mercy, is the most holy person, the yang energy is clear, is the ultimate true being in terms of incandescence, masters the Yang gate on the southernmost surface, holds the soul of humans, is infinitely brilliant, has virtue superior to all things, presides over illuminating the lives of sentient beings. born, marching day and night illuminating heaven and earth, maintaining the yin and yang. He has a warm and majestic nature, giving brilliance, everything that is illuminated is born thanks to Him. Next is the verse of the Sun God boasting about his merits: "In the sky without me, I do not have day or night, on earth without me I do not grow, every god has someone who respects me, no one respects me, the Sun God! On the nineteenth day of the first month, the Sun is born. Every family recites Buddha's name and lights a pink lamp. Whoever can recite this Sun Sutra will not be affected by drought. Whoever does not recite the Sun Sutra, the gates of hell will open right before their eyes..."

The sentences are jumbled and messy, with the full text as follows: "Tayin Bodhisattva went to the East, ten layers of nine-level hell opened, eighteen thousand Bodhisattvas, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas lined up on both sides, the Buddhas respected him, the land was cloudless, lotus flowers shot out of the water and bloomed all over the land, his head was wearing a tower of jewels, seven, and should not be recited. There are reasonable people who say these sutras are fake, but still refuse to believe them. You must know: When doing Buddhist work, only reciting Buddha's name is the greatest merit.

The Eye of Light Sutra is very short, consisting of only a few sentences as follows: "Buddha said that the Eye of Light Sutra, bright eyes are the lights of the mind, on both sides of the tower of relics, the Great Tripitaka is constantly in the future. A thousand eyes and a thousand hands are clearly visible in life. Great Wisdom Bodhisattva radiates light, Manjushri Bodhisattva rides a lion, Samantabhadra rides a royal elephant. Arhats fill the entire void of the great earth, the fog covering the eyes is immediately swept away!" The content of the Tao King Sutra (popularly known as the Kitchen God Sutra) is as follows: This sutra was spoken by the Buddha himself in India, and transmitted to China by Tripitaka masters (sic!). Mr. Tao, whose name is Dong Tru Tu Mang, monitors the behavior of everyone in the family. On the thirtieth day of each month, he reports it to heaven. Depending on good and evil behavior, heaven will bestow blessings or disasters. Mr. Tao's birthday is on the third day of the eighth lunar month. The homeowner must burn incense and light lamps to make offerings to receive blessings. Recite this sutra so students will pass, business will prosper, etc. Praying for Mr. Tao's will to live up to ninety years old. The scriptures also advise to keep the kitchen clean, not to stir pots and pans in the kitchen, not to be naked in front of the stove, not to spit, not to scold in the kitchen, not to bring slippers soiled with animal feces into the kitchen, not to bring garlic peels, chicken or duck bone feathers into the kitchen, etc.

The Pregnancy Sutra is a sutra about human formation in the mother's womb, a crude and clumsy imitation of the Buddha's Retribution Sutra. To quote an excerpt: "In the fourth month, the fetus grows, the limbs are fixed, the legs are born first, the arms are born later, the autumn, summer, spring and winter are born, two arms are born, when the arms are born, the mother's veins are drawn. When the legs are born, reaching the Huyen Quan acupuncture point, the blood vessels jump strongly, [the mother] walks on flat ground like climbing a high mountain, her knees ache"...

The Wonderful Sha Sutra is very short, the text is messy, the sentences are incomplete, the content is as follows: "Wonderful Sa Avalokiteshvara sat on a boat across the ocean, the boat was filled with a depth of five hundred (not sure what five hundred? "It is a treasure that the world's ghosts and gods do not dare to violate. Amitabha's pupil holds a golden bell and shakes it several times to empty hell. The son of Yama becomes a Buddha, and all sentient beings leave hell." We could not find any documents about the Phan Chau Sutra.

Because the house often prays for auspiciousness (goodness, luck), if you kill living beings every day, that house will immediately become a place of killing. The place of killing is the place where evil spirits gather, it is not good, [this is] very important! Therefore, one must abstain from killing living beings at home.

People who recite Buddha's name should advise their parents to recite Buddha's name and pray to be reborn in the West, but if they want their parents to decide to be reborn in the West at the time of death, they will not tell their relatives about supporting their death recitation, and the benefits and harms of blindly showing off and crying will not be possible! Therefore, we want our parents to enjoy the benefits of reciting the Buddha's name at the time of their death, without harming their mindfulness, but not telling them the benefits of reciting the Buddha's name on a daily basis, making it so that everyone recites it often, will not be possible! This is not only beneficial for parents, but it is also beneficial for current relatives and future descendants. Lam Chung supports chanting, both old and young should be like that, read the book Suc Chung Tan Luong10 and you will know for yourself (Thuong

The Hai Phat Hoc Library Department and the Bao Quoc Pagoda in Suzhou both sell that book.)

Destroying hell and destroying the blood lake are rituals performed by evil Chinese masters. They make paper models of hell and blood lake, then the monks recite sutras, draw talismans, burn talismans, run around the altar, call out to mobilize ghosts and spirits, and use a staff to pierce hell and blood lake, thinking that doing so will save the souls from hell.

Can Chung Tan Luong (instructions in taking care of the dying) is a work composed by Mr. Ly Vien Tinh with instructions on how to prepare for the moment of death and methods to support meditation to ensure that those who practice Pure Karma at the time of death do not have their mindfulness destroyed. This book is divided into four parts:

1) Mutual Strength Program: Pure Land practitioners must instruct family and friends on how to handle the person's death, how to support meditation, and how to bury the deceased so that they can maintain mindfulness.

2) Common Strength Commentary: Collection of teachings on preparation for death of ancient virtues.

3). Predicting the Benefits and Harms: Analyzes of the advantages and disadvantages of dying, such as not crying, killing, and not showing off like forcing the deceased to sit cross-legged, changing clothes, and bathing while the dying person is still breathing.

Women often experience unbearable pain when giving birth, and [if] they do not give birth for a few days, they are likely to lose their life. There are also people who have bleeding after giving birth, with all kinds of dangers, and their children have slow or rapid epilepsy, all kinds of dangers. If you are about to give birth, you should sincerely and clearly recite "namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva", do not recite silently in your mind, because the mental power of silently reciting is small, so the response is also small. At that time, he used force to push the child away. If he recited it silently, it was very likely that he would become sick due to the trapped energy. If you recite sincerely and earnestly, you will definitely avoid pain, difficulty in giving birth, bleeding after birth, the child will suffer from epilepsy, etc. Even if it is extremely difficult to give birth, or the person is about to die, you should teach the pregnant woman and the surrounding caregivers to recite Avalokiteśvara out loud together. Family members, even in other rooms, can recite it. Surely, with less than a moment of practice, you will be able to give birth peacefully. Non-Buddhists do not understand reason, are attached to a method of reverence, do not know how to base it on logic, to the point that old women reciting Buddha's name consider giving birth to be a scary thing, even if they are biological daughters or daughters-in-law, they do not dare to look at it, let alone dare to teach them to recite Quan Yin? You must know that the Bodhisattva has the mind to save suffering. Although he was about to give birth, although he was naked and impure, it was something that could not be avoided, and was not due to intentional negligence. Not only did [reciting Quan Yin at that time] not commit any sin, but it also planted great good roots for both mother and child. This meaning was taught by the Buddha in the Medicine Sutra, not my speculative opinion, I just proposed it! (The Medicine Buddha Sutra talks about the vow of merit of the Medicine Buddha, so it teaches reciting the Medicine Buddha. But everyone knows the name Quan Yin, so there is no need to recite the Medicine Buddha. Just recite the Medicine Buddha).

Women from twelve or thirteen years old to forty-eight or forty-nine years old have menstruation. Some people say, "During the sutra, do not worship or recite!" That statement does not make sense. For people whose periods are short, it ends in two or three days, while some people last up to six or seven days. People who practice must meditate without interruption, so why should they neglect their practice because of such a small birth defect? Now I say: During the sutra, you should only worship less (there should be less worship, not absolutely no worship), reciting Buddha's name, and chanting sutras as usual. You should often change dirty cloth (sanitary napkins). If your hands touch dirty cloth, you should wash them clean, do not use hands that have touched dirty things to turn the sutras or burn incense. All Buddhist dharmas are perfect, pagans only cling to the outer truths. Most people only believe in pagan words,

Truly Effective Strength: Evidence of rebirth due to careful preparation for the moment of death.

do not know the truth in Buddhism. Therefore, it is impossible for all fellow human beings to be imbued with the benefits of the Dharma.

Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva vows widely and deeply to follow the sound of relieving suffering. If you encounter tribulations such as swordsmen, water, fire, famine, pests, locusts, pestilence, drought, floods, robbers, injustice, evil beasts, poisonous snakes, demons, demons, diseases due to resentment karma, evil people... If you can develop a mind to correct your mistakes and be good, benefit yourself and others, and sincerely recite Avalokiteshvara without interruption, you will certainly be protected by His compassion and will not be in any danger. If you still keep an unhealthy heart, even if you confess your thoughts, it will only temporarily sow good roots for the future, and will not be inspired in the present. Because Buddhas and Bodhisattvas both achieve good thoughts for people, they do not achieve evil thoughts for people. If you do not have the mind to correct your mistakes towards goodness, if you are mistaken and want to recite the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the hope of achieving evil things for yourself, then you must decide not to be inspired, do not give rise to that crazy mind!

The most important thing to recite the Buddha's name is to maintain good morality, fulfill all duties, stop evil thoughts, maintain sincerity, do not do evil things, do good things, keep a good heart, speak good words, and do good things. If you have the strength to do it, then actively do it. If you can't do it, then you must also develop that kind heart. Or advise others who have the strength to do it, or see others doing it and then develop a heart of joy, and utter words of praise, it also belongs to the merit of the mind and mouth. If you cannot do it yourself, when you see someone else doing it, you become jealous, and you become a vile and evil person. You will definitely lose your blessings, shorten your life, and not get good results. You should be painfully cautious. Do not do false things to gain fame, gossip about fame and gain reputation, such behavior is truly hated by both heaven and earth, ghosts and gods. If so, it must be modified; If not, try harder.

In life, there are women who do not understand the ultimate logic, or are not filial to their parents-in-law, cheat, despise their husbands, blindly pamper their children, mistreat their servants, or are stepmothers who mistreat the children of their first wives, do not know how to filial piety and care for their parents-in-law, respect their husbands, educate their children, be generous to servants, raise and take care of their first wives' children, [not knowing these things] is truly the path of saints and sages in the world, but also the method of cultivating the roots in Buddhism. Full of this merit, by practicing Pure Karma, your honor will surely increase, you will increase your blessings, your life will be long, and when you die, you will be guided straight to the nine lotus ranks by the Buddha. You must know: If there is a cause, there will definitely be an effect. If we have sown the cause of filial piety, respect and kindness, we will enjoy the fruits of filial piety and kindness. For others is for yourself, harming others is worse than harming yourself. Therefore, we must exhaust our own duties to hope that Buddha and heaven will examine us together.

From the moment children have understanding, they are taught the virtues of filial piety, kindness, loyalty, faith, propriety, righteousness, honesty, shame, and the causes and effects of the three lives and the six paths of reincarnation, making them know that their own minds in every breath are connected to the minds of heaven, earth, ghosts, gods, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas. When an unrighteous thought arises, doing an unrighteous thing is soon seen and clearly known by heaven, earth, ghosts, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas. Just like in front of a bright mirror, an evil shadow appears that cannot be avoided, so that they know to abstain from fear and try to be good people. No matter who it is, whether it's a servant or a child, it's not allowed to hit or curse. Teach them to respect their elders and maintain their position as subordinates. We must pay attention to teaching them to cherish paper with words written on it, to cherish grain, clothes, furniture, to cherish and protect insects, and to strictly forbid snacking to avoid getting sick. If taught like that, most people will definitely become good people. If you follow your habits when you're young and don't teach anything, if you grow up and don't become ordinary people, you'll become a group of thieves and robbers. At that time, repentance is of no use! The ancients said: "The first teacher of the church, the child of the teacher" (Teach your children from childhood, teach your wife from the beginning), because training will become nature, so you must be careful from the beginning. Whether the world is peaceful or chaotic, it all originates from here; Don't think the old monk is talking nonsense, it doesn't matter, it's urgent!

Quang is old, his spirit is getting weaker, and he doesn't have the strength to reply to letters. Just because the postal route is convenient, people from near and far hear wrong names, often sending letters to ask. If you don't answer all at once, you'll feel like you're disappointing the person who asked. If we respond to each letter one by one, we really don't have the spirit [to do so]. Therefore, for printing this long letter, everything related to religious practice and the religion of establishing a family, dealing with parents, worshiping parents, and teaching children are discussed in general. If someone sends you a letter in the future, use this letter to send it back. If there is one or two special things, immediately write a few words in the letter so that both parties can understand each other's love without causing undue hardship. If you want to deeply understand the teachings of the sutras, please seek guidance from masters who have profound understanding of the high teachings. You should know that: People who deeply understand the sutras may not be able to end life and death in this life. If you want to end birth and death in this life, you should focus on praying to recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the West.

tieu_de: 2. Letter to layperson Quach Trang Ngo
tom_tat: Receiving a letter from Master Minh Dao, I know that lay people have great will. If he wants willow to be free from birth and death in this life, Quang does not hesitate to make a benchmark to mold clay and carve wood. If you want to deeply understand the scriptures and fully realize your own mind...
noi_dung:
2. Letter to layperson Quach Trang Ngo

(Year of the Republic 21 - 1932)

Receiving a letter from Master Minh Dao, I know that lay people have great will. If he wants willow to be free from birth and death in this life, Quang does not hesitate to make a benchmark to mold clay and carve wood. If you want to deeply understand the sutras and fully realize your own mind, Quang's [standard benchmark for] molding clay and carving wood cannot be used! Now, "repaying for mistakes and giving thanks for mistakes", giving lay people the Dharma name Hue Trang. Trang (莊) is glass. A Dharma of Respect is the basis for learning both worldly and extra-worldly religions. If you do not respect respect and maintain sincerity, even if you have enlightenment, you still cannot gain real benefits. Once you fall into madness, it will certainly be difficult for you to achieve perfect harmony. Heaven accepts the nature of reason and does not attach importance to cultivating it. Even though the reason is not mistaken, it is no different from evil spirits or pagans! What's more, if you accept the principle of waste, the truth that is realized will hardly be relevant. Therefore, it is said: "No noble son sees the place, only the noble son's luggage" (No precious son's place of construction, only precious son's implementation). That is the big trap for intelligent people throughout life; Not having this disease is enough to be called intelligent. Otherwise, the intelligent will be misled by the intelligent, turning into the kind of person who makes mistakes. Quang is old now, so he shouldn't send letters often anymore. Whenever I send a letter, I only use the long printed letter to respond, without explaining it to anyone in particular, so as not to be too tiring, and it's also not beneficial for the other person. Soon, there will be a new edition of the Pure Land Ten Essentials book and a long letter will arrive, no need to write letters anymore. In addition to the original Ten Essentials book, there are also several other necessary books included, which are truly the most important books for cultivating Pure Karma.

Responding to the letter of layperson Chau Manh Do asking about the four questions: "Form is not different

tieu_de: Emptiness” in the Heart Sutra
tom_tat: These few sentences are the Great Sage bringing the appearance of the Five Aggregates of Emptiness that he himself saw through and through to teach people. Form is at the top of the Five Aggregates, so it is explained thoroughly first. Saying "Form is not different from Emptiness" (Form is not different from Emptiness) is...
noi_dung:
Emptiness” in the Heart Sutra

(Year of the Republic 26 - 1937)

These few sentences are the Great Sage bringing the appearance of the Five Aggregates of Emptiness that he himself saw through and through to teach people. Form is at the top of the Five Aggregates, so it is explained thoroughly first. Saying "Form is not different from Emptiness" (Form is not different from Emptiness) is because although Form has a form that can be seen, it is an illusory appearance. Using profound Prajna wisdom to contemplate, the essence of Form is "unattainable" (completely impossible), although it exists, it is like nothingness. Not only is the essence of Form "completely impossible", but Emptiness is also "completely impossible!" Therefore, it is said "Emptiness is not different from Form" (Empty is not different from Form). Here, we are afraid that people will misunderstand that Worldly Emptiness is the form of Form and Emptiness, so we say: "Emptyness is not realistic to achieve, just as complete Form cannot be achieved!" That's because Emptiness is also a worldly dharma. Although it has no form, is empty, empty, it still has the appearance of Emptiness. In the Five Aggregates, the Emptiness of the Aggregates of Form is not the Emptiness of nothingness. Therefore, he immediately continued: "Emptiness is not different from Form" (Emptiness is not different from Form). Because of complete separation from the Emptiness of the Emptiness form, it should be said: "Emptiness is not different from Form" (Emptiness is not different from Form). Talking about this Emptiness of Emptiness is like the "completeness" of Form, which cannot be understood as empty, empty Emptiness.

Still afraid of not understanding, he said again: "Form is Emptiness, Emptiness is Form" (Form is Emptiness, Emptiness is Form), meaning: "Form is Emptiness" is impossible, "Emptiness is Form" is impossible! This form and emptiness are both revealed and destroyed. Form - Emptiness "are together" and "are separate from" Form Emptiness. If you see this, you will personally realize True Buddha Nature. Since the Aggregate of Form is like that, the four aggregates of Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness can be known accordingly; So there's no need to say any more, just say "the heron is like that" (same thing). If the Five Aggregates are like that, then all dharmas are like that. Therefore, it is said again: These Five Aggregates are all the form of Emptiness, the form of Emptiness of all dharmas, not born, not destroyed, not defiled, not clean, not increasing, not decreasing, their essence is like that, there is no need to wish according to saints - mortals, living beings - Buddha to talk anymore! Since it has no origin, why does it have destruction, as well as impurity, purity, increase, and decrease? Therefore, in the Emptiness of all dharmas, there are no five aggregates of Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, Consciousness, no six sense organs "eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind", no six sense objects "Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma", no six consciousnesses which is the Eye realm (under the word Eye, the word Consciousness is omitted), until there is no Consciousness realm. That means there is no six ordinary dharma realms.

"No ignorance, no old age until no old death" (No ignorance until no old death) are the twelve causes and conditions of the Flowing Gate. "There is no end to ignorance, there is no end to old age and death" (there is also no end to ignorance until there is no end to old age and death): These are the twelve causes and conditions of the Complete Extermination Gate. This is without the Pratyekabuddha Dharma Realm. “No suffering, origin, cessation, path”, means there is no sravaka dharma realm. “No Wisdom”: Wisdom is the last level in the Six Paramitas, so [No Wisdom] means there is no Bodhisattva Dharma Realm. “There is no attainment” (There is also no attainment): “Gain” is Bodhi, Nirvana, [ie]

There is no Buddhadharma realm. Some people understand the Emptiness in the sentence "Form is not different from Emptiness" as the True Form of True Emptiness. At first glance it seems reasonable, but on closer inspection it seems incomplete. Why is that? There are no Five Aggregates, Six Entrances, Twelve Places, and Eighteen Precepts, that is, the six ordinary dharma realms of the world; There are no Four Noble Truths, Twelve Causes and Conditions, Wisdom, and Dharma, which are the four holy dharma realms in this world. All holy and mundane dharmas are empty, so why is the Emptiness of the world also empty? Because both ordinary feelings and holy views are empty, it is possible to perfect Bodhi and return to "nothing to gain" (nothing to gain). Because there is "nothing to gain", "the mind is free from obstacles, terror, far from confusion, delusion, and achieves Nirvana" (the mind is free from entanglements, fear, far from madness, delusion, and ultimately reaches Nirvana).

This dharma is the ultimate dharma to become a Buddha of the three worlds of Buddhas. Because in the emptiness of all dharmas, there are no holy dharmas - mortals, sentient beings - Buddhas, etc., so one can go from ordinary to saintly cultivating the cause and effect, fully realizing this dharma. For example, when building a house, there must be empty space for people to live in it. If there is no room in the house, how can people live? Because of Emptiness, one can truly practice and realize. If it weren't for Mu, it wouldn't have this effect. Because in Prajna's deep wisdom, one cannot see the appearance of these kinds of views, so they are Void. Don't misunderstand and not practice is Void. If you understand and do not practice, you will destroy the Dharma of the Buddhas and will surely fall forever in Avici hell. Think carefully! This theory of Quang has some areas that are not in accordance with the explanation of the ancients, but the main meaning is not contrary to the Buddhist scriptures, it can also be said to be a kind of view "seeing the range, seeing the power, seeing the cause, seeing the wisdom"11.

tieu_de: 4. Letter of admonition to those who have just begun to study Buddhism in my hometown
tom_tat: I often say: "If you want to truly benefit from Buddhism, you must seek reverence. If you have one part of reverence, you can eliminate part of your sins and increase one part of your blessings and wisdom. If you have ten parts of reverence, you can eliminate ten parts of your sins...
noi_dung:
4. Letter of admonition to those who have just begun to study Buddhism in my hometown

I often say: "If you want to gain real benefits from Buddhism, you must seek reverence. If you have one part of reverence, you can eliminate one part of your karma and increase one part of your blessings. If you have ten parts of your respect, you can eliminate ten parts of your karma and increase your wisdom by ten parts." If you are not respectful at all, then chanting Buddhist scriptures and reciting the Buddha's name will not be without any benefits, but first of all you will have to suffer the sin of being disrespectful and falling into the three realms for many lifetimes! After all the sins have been paid, we will rely on that goodness

This sentence is based on the idiom: "A mountain range seen horizontally is a ridge, vertically seen is a peak" and the saying "the benevolent see it as benevolence, the wise see it as wisdom", which together imply: The essence is one, but depending on each person's understanding, they perceive differently.

He heard the Dharma, practiced vegetarianism, recited Buddha's name, prayed for birth in the West, and was able to escape birth and death. If in this life you run out of sincerity and devote all your devotion, then in this life you can rely on the Buddha's power to help you be reborn in the West. Once he is reborn, he will become a saint, will be free from birth and death, will forever be free from suffering, and will only enjoy such joys! People cultivating blessings or creating karma in general have no more than six senses and three karmas. The six main senses are Eyes, Ears, Nose, Tongue, Body, and Mind. The first five senses belong to the body's karma, the last sense belongs to the mind, which is the mind's karma. The three karmas are:

First, Body Karma includes three things, i.e. killing, stealing, and adultery. These three things are extremely pitiful.

a. People who study Buddhism should be vegetarian and love life. All animals know pain, are greedy for life, are afraid of death, and should not be killed. If you kill to eat, it will constitute a killing karma. In the next life, in the next life, they will surely kill them again.

b. Second is stealing. Whatever belongs to others, you should not "take it without giving it away". Stealing cheap things means losing your own personality. Stealing something valuable is harming someone's life. Stealing other people's things seems to gain comfort, [but actually] it damages your own blessings and life, losing things in your life that you should have had many times more than what you stole. If you use a scheme to usurp, or use your power to coerce and rob, or take care of [property] for someone else and then have a bad habit of taking it, it is called "theft". A thief will give birth to profligate children, and an honest person will give birth to virtuous children. That is the natural principle of cause and effect!

c. Third is adultery. Anyone who is not my own concubine, regardless of whether they are virtuous or vile, is not allowed to have sex with them. Sexual immorality is the destruction of human morality, that is, using a human body to do things to animals. If you have become an animal in your current life, you must become an animal in your next life. People consider it humiliating for a girl to sneak around with someone else, but they don't know that a boy who commits adultery is just as humiliating as a girl. Whoever commits adultery will give birth to children who are not chaste, and who wants their own children to be unchaste? Having done it yourself first, children are naturally aware of their own destiny, it is definitely difficult for them to be righteous and not evil! Not only should we not commit adultery with external lusters, but even in righteous adultery between husband and wife there should be limits. Otherwise, if you die early, you will be disabled. A greedy person will have difficulty having children, and even if they are born, it will be difficult to become human. Even if I become a human, I will still be weak and achieve nothing! People consider sexual intercourse to be fun. They don't know that it's only a moment of happiness, but they will suffer for the rest of their lives, and the suffering will spread to their children and grandchildren!

Not doing these three things is good karma in the body; if done, it is bad karma in the body.

Verbal Karma includes four: Lying, embellishing, speaking evilly, and double-talking

afternoon.

a. Lying is saying something that is not true. If you don't tell the truth, your heart won't be honest, and you'll lose a lot of your personality.

b. To talk nonsense is to say obscene words, causing others to have lustful thoughts. If an ignorant teenager listens to it for a long time, his personality will be buried by adultery, or his life will be damaged by masturbation. Even if that person does not commit adultery, he will still fall into hell. Come out of hell, or become a sow or a bitch. If one is born in the human race, one will often be a dew-eating girl, at first young and beautiful, not yet suffering much. After a long time, the sexual illness broke out and the pain was unspeakable. If you are lucky to have this mouth, why do you suffer and bring disaster to both yourself and others, not creating happiness for either yourself or others?

c. Evil speech is speaking harsh words like knives and swords, making it difficult for people to endure.

d. Talking in two directions is a two-headed shock that provokes gossip, small things cause trouble for others, big things cause chaos in the country.

If you don't do these four things, it's good karma in your mouth; if you do it, it's bad karma in your mouth.

3) Karma includes three things, i.e. greed, anger, and ignorance.

a. Lust is for money, land, and belongings, wanting to collect them all for yourself, the more you have, the less you will have.

b. Anger means whether you are right or wrong, if other people don't agree with you, you get angry and don't accept their arguments.

c. Stupidity is not complete ignorance, but even if one reads all the world's books, remembers them at a glance, opens one's mouth in chapters, but does not believe in the cause and effect of the three generations, the six paths of reincarnation, thinks that when a person dies, the soul disappears, there is no next life, etc., it is called stupidity! That kind of knowledge disturbs the water and harms the people more than a flood or a fierce beast!

Not doing these three things is good karma in the mind, doing these three things is bad karma in the mind. A person's three karma of Body - Speech - Mind are good, the merit from chanting Buddha's name is hundreds of thousands of times greater than that of a person whose three karma are all bad.

People who study Buddhism should keep a good heart, speak good words, and do good deeds. "Keeping a good heart" means that all evil thoughts that go against heaven, are unreasonable, harm others and benefit oneself are not allowed to arise. If it arises, shame immediately arises, repentance causes it to immediately disappear. All the hearts of filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, propriety, righteousness, integrity, shame, benefiting people and things are always kept, and whenever one can do it, they are eager to do it. If you can't do it, your mind often thinks about it. "Speaking good words" means saying words that are beneficial to people and things; It's not about wanting others to be happy after hearing it, which is called a good word! Such as teaching children and advising people to do good, advising people to abstain from evil, advising people to maintain moral integrity, advising people to cultivate blessings, etc. "Doing good deeds" means actively doing things to be filial to parents, respect older brothers, get along with relatives, and change customs [for the better]. Everyone chanting sutras, worshiping Buddha, reciting Buddha's name, worshiping, and all Buddhist activities must be respectful in body and mind!

People who study Buddhism at night should not sleep naked, they must wear shirts and shorts, their minds should always be as before the Buddha. You should not eat too much. No matter how delicious the rice is, you can only eat eight or nine servings [maximum]. Eating ten portions is not beneficial to people; If you eat more than a dozen portions, your internal organs will be damaged. If you often eat like that, you will definitely have a short life. If you eat too much, your mind will become dull, your body will be tired, and your digestion will not be able to keep up, and you will have flatus. Incontinence is the worst thing, the thing that causes the greatest sin. In the Buddha hall and monks' halls, everyone must be respectful; Just like burning incense is just to express your heart, but ultimately, there is no kind of incense worth considering! If you eat too much, your flatus will be extremely stinky, causing the stinking breath to poison the Three Jewels, and in the future you will be born as maggots in the dung pit. Don't eat too much and you won't have flatus!

If you use a cold substance and feel uncomfortable, if nothing happens, go to an open space to vent, wait until the smell dissipates and then go back into the room. If there's something you can't get out, you should use your strength to hold it back, in less than a moment it will disappear in your stomach. Some people say that if you don't ejaculate, you will become sick; These words are even more sinful than having sex, so do not listen to them. The Buddha's precepts did not mention this; Perhaps the ancients had healthy bodies and were not greedy for food, so this was not the case, so it was not mentioned.

If there is, Buddha must have said it. Don't say Buddha doesn't forbid it, so just release it, that's just asking for a fall, and Buddha will also find it difficult to save!

Confucius used the position of a saint to meet a monarch (king of a country) and ordinary people. When he was about to go to the palace, on the steps, he did not even dare to breathe loudly, let alone when he entered the palace to meet the king! Therefore, the book Analects writes: "Nhiep qi ascends the road, the chrysanthemum of the palace is like a field. The bottle of qi is not at all wild" (Raise the hem of the shirt to the temple, bend over like that, hold your breath as if not breathing) (Nhiep 攝: Lift. Qi 齊, read as Tu 咨12, meaning the hem of the shirt. Cuc 鞠: bend.

Binh 屏: hidden. Meaning 息: breath from the nose. When Confucius visited the king, when he was about to go to the throne, he first bowed. Because of bending over, the front hem of the shirt is longer, so we have to raise the two edges of the shirt about a meter above the ground to avoid stepping on the shirt, tripping, and being rude. Serious to the extreme, so the breath in his nose doesn't seem to escape. Let's see how cautious He is? People today are far worse than Confucius, and the king at that time was far worse than Buddha! Ejaculation is even more different than exhalation. Silently thinking, it's like the earth has no place to live, shouldn't we pay great attention?) We are ordinary people's karma in the Buddha hall of the Holy Middle Saints, Thien Trung Thien (holy of saints, heaven of heavens), where there are enough Three Jewels, how dare we not restrain and be neutral? That sin is the greatest and incomparable!

There are many people who, because they haven't read much about the ancient teachings, think that the ancients don't talk about it. I don't know what the ancients said very cleverly, calling it "steam leaking out from below". They also don't understand what that sentence means, and don't pay attention. Thirty or forty years ago, Quang often talked about this matter, but then when he asked again, people didn't know what it was! Therefore, it's best to just say "neutrality". In opera and opera, whenever cursing others for talking about letting go of drama, they say: "Your words are like releasing farts." Whenever something scares me, I don't dare to breathe loudly. How can I still have sex? Because of indulging and not abstaining, that's why we're having sex! Don't say "it's not polite to mention flatus", in fact, I want to create a way to save people from being maggots in the cesspool!

When you wake up in the morning and after urinating, you must wash your hands. Everyone who touches the body or touches the feet must wash their hands. In the summer months, trouser legs should not be baggy, they should be tied up. Casually coughing up phlegm and blowing your nose is a great loss of good fortune! Buddha's land is pure, not only in the temple hall, you are not allowed to spit or blow your nose, but even on the clean land outside.

The pronunciation of these two words in Mandarin Chinese is almost the same.

You should also not spit or blow your nose. Spitting on clean ground will create a dirty look! There are people who are careless and reckless, spitting on the ground or on the walls in the room! A beautiful room with all the ground and walls filled with talk. That person coughs up phlegm to appear bossy. Over time, he becomes sick and spits every day; The essence of food and drink turns into phlegm. If you swallow the phlegm, over time there will be no more phlegm. That is the best way to use phlegm to kill phlegm. If you can't swallow, put a sputum wipe in your sleeve, spit on it, then put it back in your sleeve. This method is both tiring and unclean. It's better than swallowing it. It's not tiring, not unclean, and will never get phlegm. This is the best way to treat phlegm.

People who study Buddhism must pay attention to every move. To recite Buddha's name, one must be sincere. If sadness ever arises in the mind, that is also the sign of good roots being discovered, don't let it happen often like that. Otherwise, you will be saddened by ghosts. Whatever happens to your liking, don't be too happy. If not, the devil will surely depend on you. When reciting Buddha's name, the eyelids should droop. You should not be so mentally stressed that the fire in your heart flares up. You may suffer from itching, headaches, etc., which need to be properly regulated. If you recite loudly, you should not try too hard to avoid getting sick. Reciting the rosary can prevent laziness, but when meditating, do not recite the rosary. Whenever you recite the rosary, your fingers move so your mind cannot be concentrated, and over time you will become ill.

Don't be in a hurry when reading sutras and books. You have to watch it many times, if you watch it too quickly, you won't be able to stop and it will be difficult to understand the meaning. The old books are deeply self-aware" (Old books are not boring to read a hundred times; read carefully, think deeply, you will know for yourself).

Confucius was a talented and intelligent saint who even read the I Ching until the margins of the book were broken three times. If we only consider the number of words, Confucius's compilation is more than ten times greater than the previous I Ching by King Wen and Cong Chau. In the I Ching, each hexagram has a general explanation of the meaning of that hexagram called Thoan. The explanation of the meaning of each Hao (i.e. a solid or broken line) in a hexagram is called Hao Tu (it is said that it was composed by Chau Cong).

The I Ching is divided into two parts: the Upper Kinh includes the first 30 hexagrams, the Lower Kinh includes the following 34 hexagrams. Ten Wings means ten wings. Most commentators say that: The Thoan part and the Hao part are like a fully formed bird, adding Thap Wings is like adding wings and feathers to make the bird more complete. In ancient times, the word Story meant classic explanation. Thoan Truyen is an explanation to clarify the meaning of Thoan Tu. The Tale of Statue is the part that explains the meaning of the Statue represented by each hexagram (Great Statue), the part that explains the symbol of each line is called the Little Statue. According to Mr. Nguyen Hien Le, Statue means form, as in the saying "In heaven a statue is formed, in the earth it is formed" (in the sky a statue is formed, in the earth a form is formed); It also has a symbolic meaning like the sentence "Thien lobes, auspicious ants, evil; saints appear" (Heaven appears in images, sees good and bad omens, saints imitate them and create symbols). The Tales System is often understood as the general explanation for each hexagram and line. Literature Stories is a part that teaches about the text of the sutras, but only focuses on the meaning of the two fruits Thuan Can and Thuan Khon. Theory of the Qua The story teaches about the meaning of eight simple hexagrams (Can, Kham, Can, Chan, Ton, Ly, Khon, Doai). 5. Letter to teacher Minh Bon

(Year of the Republic 16 - 1927)

The common disease of the entire world today is relying on public gain for private gain, making the people miserable, the country in danger, and constant war. We become monks as Buddhist disciples, of course we must take the Buddha's equality, great compassion, as our ambition, we should not forever maintain the arrogance and arrogance of lay people, looking down on everything, behaving indifferently, not following the old ways. We must think that we are protected by heaven and earth, and educated by our parents. If we do not imitate the hearts of heaven, earth, and parents, we will become people who disobey heaven and earth, causing profound humiliation to the parents. Linh Nham16 is an ancient ashram that is one thousand and one hundred years old. After the chaos, it became a desolate place. Although there are still a few buildings left, there are no people to support them and they are still in decline. Fortunately, at the end of Quang Tu's reign, the great dharma protector named Nghiem heard Master Chan17's voice and welcomed him. That's because I hope the Master will restore the ashram. Although Master Chan accepted it, he was afraid of the constraints and could not personally lead it. Last year, the 18th Dharma Master came here. He was happy to find someone, so he explained everything and personally took him to the mountain to become an Abbot. They also invited officials and scholars to speak up to clarify and transform this pagoda

Linh Nham Pagoda's full name is Linh Nham Son Tu, located in Ngo Huyen, To Chau. Starting from Tu Khong Luc Ngoan, he turned his private house into a pagoda, but it was very small. By the reign of Thien Giam (502-519) during the reign of Emperor Wu of Liang, the pagoda was expanded and named Tu Phong Tu. According to the Dai Ai Sutra (translated by Truc Phap Ho), that place is the enlightenment ashram of Tri Tich Bodhisattva. During the Thien Bao period (742-755) of Tang Huyen Tong's reign, the founder of the Thien Thai sect, Dao Tuan, once practiced Phap Hoa Samadhi at this temple. In the early Song Dynasty, the pagoda became an academy of precepts of Luat Tong. During the Nguyen Phong period (1078-1085), the pagoda became a Zen monastery. The pagoda burned down, leaving only a stone tower remaining in the 18th year of Van Lich (1600) during the reign of Ming Than Tong. After being restored, the pagoda was burned down again by Thai Binh Thien Quoc rebels. It was not until the third year of Tuyen Thong (1911) that monk Chan Dat stood up to rebuild the pagoda as it is today.

Master Chan (True Master) here is the monk Chan Dat, the abbot who had the merit of restoring Linh Nham in the third year of Tuyen Thong (1911).

Dharma Master Gioi Tran (1878-1948) was from Han Xuyen, Hubei province, surnamed Khuu, nicknamed Dich Ngo, became a monk at the age of nineteen, specialized in asceticism, lived in Chung Nam mountain, wholeheartedly practicing Zen. After that, he specialized in practicing Buddha's name. During the reign of Guangxu, the Master went to Ketuc Mountain in Yunnan to practice the Banzhou Buddha Recitation method. In the third year of the Republic of China (1914), the Master came to open Hoa Nghiem University in Hangzhou. Later, the Master went into seclusion at Phat Than Pagoda in Thuong Thuc, secretly cultivating Pure Karma. In the ninth year of the Republic of China (1920), together with Lieu Tran, Tu Chau, etc., they established Hoa Nghiem University at Cuu Lien Pagoda in Hankou. The monk once held the position of Abbot of Linh Nham Pagoda for a period of time. The Master passed away in the 37th year of the Republic of China (1948) at Cung Truc Pagoda in Kunming, at the age of 71 years old, with 53 years of teachings. Previous works include Hoa Nghiem Nhat Trich, Hoa Nghiem That Xu Cuu Hoi Do, Lien Xa Minh Huan, Tinh Tong Essential Ngu, etc.

become a permanent place in the ten directions. Teacher Gioi's moral character, career, and reputation are all excellent, truly worthy of being a model for his successors. What are you interested in? You should only follow the usual Pure Land rules and do not display any other fancy designs. Ashoka Pagoda is located on Ashoka Mountain in Jinan District, Zhejiang Province. According to legend, in the second year of Taikang (281) in the reign of Emperor Wu of Jin, a man named Luu Tat Ha of Tinh Chau fell into a coma in the mountains. Hui Dat then built a temple to worship the tower. That is the origin of Ashoka Pagoda. Even though she has a Pure Karma practice that can correspond to Buddha's, and is guided by Buddha, but when she encounters those actions that destroy her pure thoughts, she will definitely still stay in the Sa Ba world, from this earthly life to the next, still reincarnated in the six realms. Therefore, advising relatives to recite Buddha's name is the most urgent task.

Quang is an ordinary monk who only knows rice and porridge. He cannot benefit her from the wonderful principles of the sutras. 7. Letter replying to Master Huyen Tu

(Year of the Republic 23 - 1934)

The basic tenet of reciting the Buddha's name is to have true faith (i.e. Faith), to make earnest vows (i.e. Vow), to diligently uphold the Buddha's name (i.e. Hanh. Faith - Vow - Hanh is the main tenet of reciting the Buddha's name). The best method of reciting Buddha's name is "taking in all six senses, followed by pure recitation". "Receiving all six senses" is the mind reciting Buddha's name focusing on the Buddha's name, that is, capturing the sense of mind. The mouth must recite clearly and distinctly, which means capturing the true sense. The ears must listen clearly and distinctly, that is, to absorb the ear sense. If you combine these three senses into the Buddha's name, your eyes will definitely not be able to see in confusion. When reciting Buddha's name, your eyes must be half-closed, that is, your eyelids should be lowered, do not open them wide. If your eyes are taking photos, your nose won't smell too much, which means your nose can also take photos. The body must be respectful, that is, the body must also be photographed. If the six senses are not scattered, the mind will not have false thoughts. Only thinking about Buddha will be pure thoughts. If the six senses are not taken care of, even if you recite the Buddha's name, your mind will still be filled with false thoughts, and it will be difficult to get real benefits! If you can constantly meditate on all six senses, it is called "continuous pure mindfulness". Constantly maintaining pure recitation is one undisturbed mind, and gradually one will attain Buddha-recitation samadhi.

They were afraid that future generations would study [Buddha], so they tried their best to discourage the later generations of students so that they would not know the Buddha Dharma; But how can we stop someone who has some capacity! It's just that they use that trick so that people with middle-class nature will not be able to personally immerse themselves in the Dharma!

Now I give each of them a Dharma name, please divide the letter and give it to them, or bring the main ideas in this letter [rewrite and send] for each person to copy for themselves. There is no picture [attached], I just want to worship Buddha and recite Buddha's name. What's the use of using my picture? The current world has become extremely chaotic, natural disasters have never been more numerous than now. In these times, everyone must develop a heart of appreciation, everyone must strive to cultivate the way of being human in morality and daily behavior, and practice the Pure Land dharma. This is called "cultivating the truth in the mundane world, living in the mundane world, learning the Dharma, Buddha Dharma and worldly Dharma both practice together". If in past lives we had not planted good roots, the name of Buddha would still have been difficult to hear! If you don't actively practice, you will end up going to the treasure mountain and coming back empty-handed. You are betraying Buddha's grace and your own spirituality!

tieu_de: 9. Reply to the letter of layperson Chau Tung Nghieu
tom_tat: Now I have a question, I request the old magician to kindly clarify. The disciple has been vegetarian and chanting Buddha's name for many years. Because people who believe in Buddha are protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions and three worlds, the heavenly dragons and eight sects, and mighty divine kings often follow...
noi_dung:
9. Reply to the letter of layperson Chau Tung Nghieu

(Attached is the original letter of inquiry, Republic year 20 - 1931)

Now I have a question, I request the old magician to kindly clarify. The disciple has been vegetarian and chanting Buddha's name for many years. Because people who believe in Buddha are protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions and three worlds, the heavenly dragons, the eight divisions, and the great powers of divine kings often follow and support, the evil karma of previous lives is gradually destroyed, even if there is resentment, it cannot be harmed. That is exactly what the Buddhist scriptures said, it is definitely not a lie. Yet in March, I received news from my mother in Shanghai, saying that Mrs. Truong strongly believed in Buddha, had been a vegetarian for more than twenty years, often came to Lay Si Lam to listen to the sutras, and advised everyone to chant the Buddha's name and be vegetarian, with great compassion and good will. Who would have thought that one day, while bringing vegetarian food to a monk, he was hit by a car and killed on the way. After that, the traffic police department brought the body back. It was not until three days later that the family's children and grandchildren learned about it and came to pick it up and shroud it. After hearing this story, I was extremely frightened. To this day, my doubts cannot be resolved! Furthermore, the people in the Buddha Association were all uneasy when they heard this. That's why I specially sent this letter, asking the old magician to explain why she was so miserable when she died? Will she finally be reborn in the West? Please explain this clearly so that everyone can feel secure in reciting Buddha's name and be extremely grateful for your kindness.

Receiving the letter, I know that you still do not really understand the principles of Buddhism. From beginningless time until now, we have created limitless and boundless negative karma. The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches: "If evil karma had a physical form, the ten directions would not be able to contain it" (If evil karma had a physical form, the ten directions would not be able to contain it). You must know: If a religious person is sincere and does not lie, he or she can change karma and turn heavy retribution in the next life into light retribution in this life. Ordinary people's physical eyes can only see the present good and bad truths, they cannot know the cause and effect of the past and the future! Like that old woman who practiced diligently for many years, one day she died tragically, perhaps because that suffering would destroy the karma of the three evil paths she had created, and be born in the good path. If you have true faith and vows in life, you can also be reborn in the West. But we do not have the Tha Tam path eye, we do not dare to guess whether we are deciding to be reborn or not deciding to be reborn. We can only say decisively: "If you do good, you will definitely receive good reward, if you do evil, you will definitely receive evil reward."

Doing good and getting evil in return is the retribution of bad karma in previous lives, not the retribution of good karma in the present life. When you saw that old man receiving that retribution, in your heart you must have had the wrong view that "doing good is useless, doing good is not worth doing", so you were startled and suspicious. How is such knowledge different from someone who has not heard the Buddha Dharma? If you deeply believe in Buddha's words, you will not have that panic and doubtful attitude because of this matter; Because, the story of cause and effect overlaps endlessly. This cause has not yet [formed into] the retribution, the other effect has ripened first. Just like growing rice, the rice that ripens early is harvested first; Like being in debt, the one with the power drags you away first.

In ancient times, there were people who did good deeds throughout their lives, but when they were about to die, they died miserably to satisfy their karma, and in their next life they would be honored by wealth and honor. Like a monk at Duc Vuong Pagoda (A Duc Vuong Pagoda) in the Song Dynasty, who wanted to repair the shrine of relics, thinking that Nghi Than Vuong was powerful, he went to donate to the grave, but could not collect much, became extremely angry, so he used a hammer to cut off his hand in front of the shrine of relics, bleeding to death. Right at that time, the king gave birth to a child who cried endlessly. The nanny took her out to play. When she came to the place where the relic tower was hanging, she immediately stopped. After leaving, she cried again. [The nanny] took the picture down. The nanny often held that picture in front of her face and never cried. Hearing that, the king was surprised, so he sent someone to Duc Vuong pagoda to ask the monk that the child's birth date was exactly the day [the monk] cut off his hand and bled to death. The king then repaired the relic palace alone. When [the child turned] twenty years old, Ninh Tong died, having no children, so that young man succeeded him, and became emperor for forty-one years, that is, Tong Ly Tong (1225-1265). That monk's death was also tragic. If he hadn't often cried incessantly and stopped seeing the drawing of the relics, who would have known that the child was the reincarnation of the monk who tragically cut off his hand and died?
